mcqs.q: Which is an objective of tooth preparation (G.V. Black)?
opts: Remove defects, protect the pulp, withstand masticatory forces and restore esthetically
Remove as much tooth as possible
mcqs.explain: Objectives: remove all defects, protect the pulp, form a preparation that resists fracture under masticatory forces, and allow esthetic/functional restoration.

mcqs.q: Tooth preparation is divided into:
mcqs.explain: Preparation has an initial stage (outline, resistance, retention, convenience) and a final stage (remove infected dentin, pulp protection, secondary R&R, finishing, cleaning/sealing).

mcqs.q: The FIRST step of the initial stage is:
mcqs.explain: Step 1 is establishing the outline form and initial depth — placing the margins where they will be in the final preparation.

mcqs.q: A principle of outline form is to:
opts: Remove all weakened enamel and include all caries
Place margins on a cusp tip
mcqs.explain: Outline form should remove all weakened enamel, include all caries, and place margins to allow good finishing of the restoration.

mcqs.q: To preserve marginal-ridge strength, the remaining ridge should be greater than:
opts: 1.6 mm for a premolar and 2 mm for a molar
mcqs.explain: The remaining marginal ridge should be >1.6 mm in premolars and >2 mm in molars to avoid fracture from undermining.

mcqs.q: To preserve cusp strength, the bucco-lingual width of the preparation should be no more than:
mcqs.explain: Minimizing bucco-lingual width (≤¼ of the inter-cuspal distance) prevents weakening of the cusps and increases tooth resistance.

mcqs.q: Enameloplasty is:
opts: Reshaping the enamel surface with rotary instruments (to eliminate a shallow fissure)
mcqs.explain: Enameloplasty is reshaping the enamel surface with suitable rotary cutting instruments, used when indicated within the outline-form criteria.

mcqs.q: Primary RESISTANCE form is the shape that enables the restoration and tooth to:
mcqs.explain: Primary resistance form is the shape/placement that best enables both the restoration and the tooth to withstand masticatory forces without fracture.

mcqs.q: A feature of primary resistance form is:
opts: Relatively flat floors and a box-shaped design
mcqs.explain: Resistance-form features include relatively flat floors, a box-shaped design and adequate (not over-extended) dimensions.

mcqs.q: Primary RETENTION form is the shape that:
opts: Resists displacement or removal of the restoration by tipping/lifting forces
mcqs.explain: Retention form resists displacement/removal of the restoration by tipping or lifting forces.

mcqs.q: The primary retention feature of an amalgam Class I preparation is:
opts: Occlusal convergence of the walls (slight undercut)
mcqs.explain: Amalgam Class I retention is provided by occlusal convergence of the walls, creating a slight undercut that locks in the restoration.

mcqs.q: Convenience form provides for:
opts: Adequate observation, accessibility and ease of operation
mcqs.explain: Convenience form is the shape giving adequate observation, accessibility and ease in preparing and restoring the tooth.

mcqs.q: In the FINAL stage, which step removes the deepest caries?
opts: Removal of any remaining infected dentin and/or old restorative material
mcqs.explain: In the final stage, remaining infected dentin and old restorative material are removed (Step 5), followed by pulp protection if needed.

mcqs.q: INFECTED dentin should be:
opts: Removed — it is soft and bacteria-laden
mcqs.explain: Infected (outer) dentin is soft and full of bacteria and must be removed; affected (inner) dentin is firmer, bacteria-free and can be left near the pulp.

mcqs.q: AFFECTED dentin differs from infected dentin in that it is:
opts: Firmer, bacteria-free and remineralisable (may be left near the pulp)
mcqs.explain: Affected dentin is the inner, firmer, demineralized-but-bacteria-free layer; it can remineralize and may be left near the pulp to avoid exposure.

mcqs.q: Two close preparations should be connected if they are less than:
mcqs.explain: When two preparations are very close (less than 0.5 mm apart), they should be connected to avoid leaving a weak isthmus.

mcqs.q: To preserve cusp strength, the cavity margin should NOT terminate:
opts: On an extreme eminence such as a cusp height
mcqs.explain: Margins should avoid extreme eminences (e.g. cusp tips); placing a margin there weakens the cusp.

mcqs.q: Pulp protection during preparation is guided by the:
opts: Remaining dentin thickness (RDT) — less RDT means more pulp risk
mcqs.explain: The remaining dentin thickness (RDT) over the pulp determines the need for protection — less RDT means greater pulp damage risk.

mcqs.q: Restricting the pulpal depth during outline form helps to:
opts: Avoid unnecessary pulp damage and preserve tooth strength
mcqs.explain: Restricting the pulpal depth is one of the outline-form criteria, protecting the pulp and conserving tooth structure.

mcqs.q: The completed restoration should ultimately:
opts: Restore form and function and withstand masticatory forces
mcqs.explain: The final restoration restores esthetics/function and, with proper resistance form, withstands masticatory forces.

mcqs.q: Which is part of the INITIAL preparation stage?
opts: Outline, resistance, retention and convenience form
mcqs.explain: The initial stage comprises outline form, primary resistance form, primary retention form and convenience form.

mcqs.q: The final procedures include cleaning, inspecting and:
mcqs.explain: The last step is the final procedures of cleaning, inspecting and sealing the prepared cavity.

saqs.q: List the four steps of the INITIAL preparation stage.
saqs.a: Outline form, primary resistance form, primary retention form, convenience form.

saqs.q: State the principles of outline form.
saqs.a: Remove all weakened enamel, include all caries, and place margins for good finishing.

saqs.q: Define primary resistance form and a feature of it.
saqs.a: The shape that lets the restoration and tooth withstand masticatory forces without fracture; feature: flat floors / box shape.

saqs.q: Define primary retention form and give the amalgam Class I feature.
saqs.a: The shape that resists displacement of the restoration; for amalgam Class I: occlusal convergence of the walls.
Infected: outer, soft, bacteria-laden → must be removed. Affected: inner, firmer, demineralized but bacteria-free → remineralisable, may be left near the pulp.

saqs.q: List the marginal-ridge thickness limits and bucco-lingual width rule.
saqs.a: Marginal ridge >1.6 mm (premolar), >2 mm (molar); bucco-lingual width ≤¼ of the inter-cuspal distance.

saqs.q: List the final-stage steps of tooth preparation.
saqs.a: Remove infected dentin/old restoration, pulp protection, secondary resistance & retention, finish external walls, final cleaning/inspecting/sealing.
